title: An erase held undrawn records the erase as epoch 0, so the first pass after a later draw disconnects a reconnected Apple Health again, with no message
evidence: Checkpoint 4 look-back; the residual S45 names. ios/HealthRoadmap/Health/AppleHealthSync+Owed.swift:18 (erased) sets memory.eraseSeen = EraseSeen(epoch: store.myData?.eraseEpoch ?? 0, source:). While the erase is held with no drawing, myData is nil (RecordStore+Readable.swift:16 reads readable?.drawn?.myData), so it records epoch 0. Once the record is drawn (by PR 1681's redraw at foreground or midnight, S45, if merged; otherwise after a later draw), followErase (AppleHealthSync.swift:253-271) builds EraseSeen with the drawn eraseEpoch N > 0, and EraseGate.decide (HealthSyncMemory.swift:216-220) answers .disconnect when connected, since N > 0 and the source matches. If the person tapped Connect while held, Health is disconnected again and its owed deletes run (AppleHealthSync.swift:262-269), with no words on screen. No copy made since the erase is deleted: none can be made while held (applyInTurn refuses, RecordStore.swift:399; Health writes read the erased record). It only undoes that reconnect. Fix: followErase adopts the new epoch when eraseSeen.epoch is 0 and the source matches. That change sits in HealthSyncMemory.swift's EraseGate, off-limits to this thread: owner's ruling. US-72 AC10; US-25 AC16f
